That request was immediately refused by United and, while there was faint hope that a compromise could have been found to keep him at Old Trafford, he has stayed away ever since.

He has been training in Madrid in recent days ahead of a move to Real Madrid, and has taken to social media to bid farewell to the Red Devils after six years at the club.

It has been revealed that gabriel’s announcement is thought to have caught United by surprise, with the club first learning about it when the video appeared on social media. It’s understood that United haven’t heard from the player’s family since he was last seen at Carrington in September.

Despite his clear intention to sign for Madrid, United’s stance hasn’t changed and they still believe it will require FIFA’s approval for any move to go through.

Sources indicate that 'Dear Manchester United,' he began. 'I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with massive dreams.

JJ Gabriel has confirmed his Manchester United exit online ahead of a move to Real Madrid.

The 16-year-old penned a speech to the club, which he read out in a post (Instagram/jjnr10).

In a recent development, 'Here I grew as a player and as a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award. You gave me moments I’ll always treasure.

'To every coach, member of staff, team-mate, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow. As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything. JJ.'.

Recent findings suggest that daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed Madrid's growing confidence in securing the free-scoring starlet back in September. Gabriel has now secured a European Union passport through his mother's Cypriot heritage, and sources familiar with the situation believe a switch is imminent.

It is understood Gabriel will play for Madrid's Castilla team, which plays in Spain's third division, as well as in the Youth League.

Industry observers note that gabriel broke a series of records playing for United youth teams, including becoming the youngest player to feature in the Under-18s. Gabriel was 14 and scored twice on his debut.

United's decline since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson led to Gabriel's family seeking an exit.

O'Cearuill senior has been described as a fiercely ambitious, pushy parent. He is credited with the decision to get JJ out of United in an attempt to fast-track his career.

According to recent reports, the family had previously flirted with other major European clubs, including Barcelona. Gabriel even went on a tour of the Spanish club's ground – and was photographed with superstar forward Lamine Yamal.

Former United head coach Michael Carrick remarked of Gabriel: 'He's a young boy, he's 15 and the biggest (thing) for me definitely and as a club point of view is looking after our younger players – their welfare, their wellbeing, their exposure.

Harry Kane’s surgery likely to force Bayern Munich’s hand on January 2027 transfer market

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (776 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Harry Kane’s serious injury has presented Bayern Munich with a problem that extends considerably beyond the loss of their leading striker.
  • Kane underwent successful surgery overnight and is expected to remain sidelined well into 2027.
  • The question now concerns how Bayern intend to compensate for a player who functions simultaneously as a goalscorer, creator, and central reference point in Kompany’s system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Harry Kane’s serious injury has presented Bayern Munich with a problem that extends considerably beyond the loss of their leading striker. The English international is expected to miss several months after suffering a syndesmosis ligament tear during Friday evening’s 1-1 Bundesliga draw against Cologne, leaving Vincent Kompany with an increasingly depleted collection of attacking options.

Kane underwent successful surgery overnight and is expected to remain sidelined well into 2027. The Ballon d’Or winner has registered four Bundesliga goals and seven assists this season, making his absence particularly problematic given the considerable influence he exerts over Bayern’s attacking buildup.

The question now concerns how Bayern intend to compensate for a player who functions simultaneously as a goalscorer, creator, and central reference point in Kompany’s system. The increasingly uncomfortable answer is that a winter transfer may soon become unavoidable.

There is a certain irony surrounding Bayern’s current predicament. Get German Football News examined the club’s squad construction extensively in its 2026/27 Bundesliga tactical preview, noting that Bayern had repeatedly demonstrated an ability to function successfully with comparatively small squads. The German record champions entered the campaign with considerable attacking versatility, even if the options available to Kompany were not always distributed evenly across individual positions.

That flexibility has now been stretched to its limits.

Sources indicate that serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari both sustained significant injuries during Bayern’s October encounter with Borussia Dortmund. The former is recovering from a hamstring problem and is not expected to return before the new year. Saibari suffered a syndesmosis injury of his own, requiring surgery and leaving him unavailable until well into 2027. Both would otherwise represent credible alternatives to Kane. Both Gnabry (Germany) and Saibari (Morocco) have experience operating as central attackers for their respective national teams.

Neither, however, is presently available to provide Kompany with a solution.

Sources indicate that jamal Musiala’s return against Cologne at least restores some attacking creativity, but the German international is only beginning to regain competitive rhythm after another lengthy injury absence. More importantly, Musiala is not a conventional striker and would be unlikely to replace Kane’s physical presence or finishing responsibilities.

Bayern must therefore look elsewhere.

Luis Diaz appears to offer the most plausible short-term answer. The Colombian is nearing a return from his thigh injury and could become available for Wednesday’s Champions League encounter against Lille. His extensive experience under Jürgen Klopp at Liverpool makes him an especially interesting candidate.

During Klopp’s final season at Anfield, Diaz occasionally operated as a central attacker. Deploying Diaz centrally would nevertheless produce another problem. The Colombian has been Bayern’s principal left-sided attacking outlet. Removing him from that position would oblige Kompany to find another solution on the wing, particularly with Alphonso Davies still recovering from injury.

Nathaniel Brown has already demonstrated considerable positional flexibility, but asking the summer signing to assume yet another attacking assignment would hardly constitute an ideal long-term arrangement.

Lennart Karl represents another possibility.

According to recent reports, the 18-year-old operated centrally after Kane departed against Cologne, occasionally exchanging positions with Tom Bischof. The youngster is not a natural centre-forward and stands at only five feet, six inches.

It has been revealed that his strengths lie in his technical ability, movement between the lines, and capacity to attack opponents while facing goal. Operating with his back to goal against physically imposing central defenders is an entirely different assignment.

The remaining options are hardly reassuring. Nineteen-year-old Noah Codjo-Evora made his Bundesliga debut against Cologne, while highly regarded 16-year-old Bastian Assomo has attracted attention through his extraordinary goalscoring performances for Germany’s U17 national team.

Both are promising prospects, but neither should be expected to carry Bayern’s attacking responsibilities during a demanding Bundesliga and Champions League campaign. The shortage of established alternatives places sporting director Max Eberl in an increasingly difficult position.

According to recent reports, bayern have traditionally approached the winter transfer market cautiously, preferring to avoid expensive short-term solutions whenever possible. The prospect of injured players gradually returning after the winter break also provides a reasonable argument against making a hasty decision.

In a recent development, A January addition would not necessarily have to be an expensive replacement for Kane. A versatile forward capable of operating centrally while providing cover across the attacking line could offer Kompany considerably greater flexibility without compromising the club’s longer-term plans.

It has been revealed that bayern may still find a way to cope without Kane over the coming weeks. Whether they can reasonably expect to do so for several months without additional reinforcements is an entirely different question.

At this stage, a January signing looks less like a luxury and increasingly like a necessity.

Mikey Moore reflects on conquering his nerves after Bundesliga breakthrough

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (610 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that tottenham Hotspur loanee Mikey Moore has expressed his relief after scoring his first Bundesliga goal in Friday evening’s 1-1 draw between Bayern Munich and FC Cologne.
  • Moore nevertheless displayed remarkable composure in the 12th minute at the Allianz Arena.
  • Industry observers note that the goal represented a significant breakthrough for an attacker whose performances had attracted mounting criticism during his first months in Germany.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that tottenham Hotspur loanee Mikey Moore has expressed his relief after scoring his first Bundesliga goal in Friday evening’s 1-1 draw between Bayern Munich and FC Cologne. The 19-year-old Englishman admitted afterward that his prolonged wait for a goal had left him concerned about how he might react when presented with a scoring opportunity.

Moore nevertheless displayed remarkable composure in the 12th minute at the Allianz Arena. After initiating an attacking combination involving Linton Maina and Said El Mala, the youngster received the ball back from the latter, rounded Bayern goalkeeper Jonas Urbig, and finished confidently to give the visitors an early lead.

Industry observers note that the goal represented a significant breakthrough for an attacker whose performances had attracted mounting criticism during his first months in Germany. Moore subsequently came close to scoring again after halftime and contributed to several other promising attacking sequences.

Get German Football News awarded Moore its Player of the Match distinction and a 7/10 rating for his efforts against the German record champions.

Industry observers note that the performance came at an vital point in Moore’s Bundesliga development. As GGFN reported earlier this month, Cologne head coach René Wagner had continued to defend the Tottenham prospect despite inconsistent performances and several appearances on the substitutes’ bench.

Wagner repeatedly emphasized that Moore possessed the necessary attacking qualities to succeed in Germany, suggesting that a single decisive moment might provide the confidence required to establish himself.

Moore’s struggles subsequently prompted speculation that Tottenham might terminate his season-long loan during the January transfer window. Get German Football News examined the rumours and the considerable doubts surrounding an early recall following Cologne’s defeat to Bayer Leverkusen.

Friday’s performance provided welcome justification for that patience.

Moore covered 12.5 kilometres against Bayern, more than any of his Cologne teammates, and contested eleven individual duels. His attacking contributions also demonstrated the potential of a partnership that Wagner has been eager to develop.

According to recent reports, GGFN first reported on the coach’s enthusiasm for a Moore–El Mala combination in September. The two youngsters have subsequently required time to develop an understanding, but their cooperation against Bayern produced some of Cologne’s most dangerous attacking moments.

Sporting director Thomas Kessler praised Moore afterward, emphasizing that the club had always recognized his potential despite the difficulties accompanying his adaptation to German football.

It has been revealed that the 19-year-old nevertheless acknowledged that one successful performance would not be sufficient. Cologne remain without a Bundesliga victory in five matches, and both player and club will need to build upon their encouraging evening in Munich.

“It was a really good feeling,” Moore – as quoted by Kicker – noted after Friday’s match. “We combined really well, and then I tried to stay calm at the end. I hadn’t scored before, so I was afraid I might panic in front of goal.”.

Moore also discussed the developing understanding between himself and El Mala.

Sources indicate that “It takes a little time to understand each other perfectly,” the Englishman explained. “He’s extremely quick and loves making runs in behind the opposition defence.”.

Kessler praised the youngster’s development while emphasizing the importance of patience.

Industry observers note that “You could see why we signed him,” the Cologne sporting director explained. “Mikey has repeatedly shown promising signs. But if we want to be successful with young players, that takes time. It’s nice that Mikey was able to crown his performance with a goal, It’s a step in the right direction.”.

Moore himself remained determined to build on his breakthrough.

“I’ve settled in well,” the 19-year-old said. “Now I have to back it up.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the upcoming Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

Memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

Industry observers note that thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4.

In a recent development, in five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

In a recent development, “That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”.

Industry observers note that in the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” remarked Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”.

In a recent development, there was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

Industry observers note that to lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r.

It has been revealed that A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

It has been revealed that even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

Recent findings suggest that throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

It has been revealed that despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

Recent findings suggest that in keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN.

Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

“Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” said Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”.

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

“He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”.

Couple that with his impressive chemistry with newly introduced arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

In a recent development, “Every game starts at 0-0, but clearly Arsenal are favourites. We’ll need to show our strength and ability to be competitive. We’ll approach the game with determination and pride as we try to get a positive result.

According to recent reports, “We have to turn over a fresh leaf. We face a different challenge tomorrow. We’ll need to put in a technically excellent performance and be able to defend better than we did against Como and Inter.”.

These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

It has been revealed that arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

According to recent reports, “It will be a really tough place, I’ve been in that stadium before, I know the atmosphere they create, their record at home is really, really strong. They have a very experienced manager, a lot of players that played in the league as well, so we know the challenge ahead. We are prepared and we’re ready to go.”.

Two matches kicked off at 5.45pm, and with just under half an hour to go:.

The visitors are still without Cristhian Mosquera, who picked up an injury against Aston Villa, and Jurrien Timber – though the right-back has rejoined first-team training and travelled with the squad to Italy. William Saliba remains their only long-term absentee as he recovers from a back injury.

Naples have a few more players out of action. As well as McTominay, centre-back Alessandro Buongiorno is still sidelined following a knee procedure over summer and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa is missing with a groin injury.

Strikers Giovane and David Neres are dealing with hernia and knee problems respectively, while youngster Luca Marianucci is on his way back after a knee injury in pre-season.

Napoli have not started the season particularly well, losing two of their three Serie A games so far. But they do have a player who has a long history of hurting Arsenal: the great Kevin De Bruyne. The former Manchester City midfielder has been directly involved in 12 goals in his last 17 starts against Arsenal across all competitions (8 goals, 4 assists), including five in his most recent three (3 goals, 2 assists). Now 35 though, he is not the force he once was.

Here is how the hosts are lining up tonight:.

Meret; Olivera, Marin, Rrahmani, Di Lorenzo; De Bruyne, Lobotka, Gilmour; Santos, Hojlund, Politano.

Subs: Favasuli, Badiashile, Neres, Contini, Lucca, Vergara, Beukema, Milinkovic-Savic, Spinazzola.

It has been revealed that arsenal’s Champions League campaign last year ended in the most agonising of penalty shoot-out defeats but that should not detract from the brilliance of their run to the final. Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

Industry observers note that mikel Arteta has made four changes to the team that defeated Chelsea on Sunday. Piero Hincapie comes in for Riccardo Calafiori, Mikel Merino for Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz.

Good evening from a very sticky and humid Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, where the temperature is just a little too high to be pleasant. Perhaps that will change in time for kick-off. Perhaps it’s not relevant if I feel a bit uncomfortable in my jeans. Readers can make their own minds up on that….

Industry observers note that anyway, this should be a fun game. The atmosphere is usually pretty intense in this part of the world and they will be up for this one. The absence of Scott McTominay due to a minor heart problem is good news for Arsenal, who are likely to make a few changes to the team that beat Chelsea so impressively at the weekend.

Welcome back to another night of Champions League football direct to your mobile/desktop/electronic device of your choosing!

Both Aston Villa and Manchester City got off to winning starts last night, beating Club Brugge and Porto respectively. Other fun fixtures included Real Madrid beating Inter Milan, getting Jose Mourinho his own winning return in Europe with Madrid. Now it’s Arsenal’s turn.

After falling at the final hurdle last season – losing on penalties to Paris St-Germain in Budapest – they have travelled to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, hoping to take the first step of a new attempt to claim their white whale.

In a recent development, their Italian hosts have not had the smoothest start to the 2026-27 campaign, settling under fresh manager Massimiliano Allegri. While Antonio Conte guided them to a second-place finish in Serie A last season, they have only managed one win from three league games – losing to Como and Inter Milan – meaning that they right now sit 12th in the league.

They were eliminated after the league phase of the Champions League last year, finishing to 30th out of 36 teams, and will surely be looking to improve on that poor performance this season.

It has been revealed that as for the Premier Champions, who have started their domestic season with a 100 per cent record, they will have their eyes on the prize from the get-go. They were formidable in the league phase last year, winning all eight matches and scoring 23 goals while conceding just four.

We will be getting team news shortly and will be bringing you the pre-match updates as they come.

Despite the carnage at UK airports this week, Sam Dean has made it to Naples and will be bringing us updates from the continent.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nella Serie A 2025-26 l’olandese aveva segnato quattro reti in 29 presenze; ora conta anche quattro assist.

Tijjani Noslin ha segnato quattro gol e servito quattro assist con la Lazio: per partecipazioni alle reti in Serie A è secondo solo ad Adrien Rabiot. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, Il francese del Milan conta cinque gol e quattro assist, uno in più dell’olandese nel totale.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Noslin ha realizzato le sue quattro reti in 10 partite di campionato. Sono tante quante quelle segnate nelle 29 presenze dell’intera Serie A 2025-26. Solo una volta ha fatto meglio, arrivando a cinque gol nella stagione 2023-24.

It has been revealed that il suo percorso da rider a realizzatore si è sviluppato nell’arco di cinque anni, dal 2021 a oggi, passando attraverso difficoltà e successi. Ora i suoi gol e i suoi assist lo collocano tra i giocatori più incisivi del campionato, non soltanto della Lazio.

In a recent development, il dato più alto di Noslin per partecipazioni alle reti in una stagione di Serie A resta quello del 2023-24. Con l’Hellas Verona, in 17 partite, fu coinvolto in nove gol: cinque segnati e quattro assist.

It has been revealed that con i quattro gol e i quattro assist attuali è a quota otto. Ha dunque già eguagliato il numero di passaggi decisivi registrato in quella stagione, mentre gli manca una partecipazione a una rete per raggiungerne il totale.

Recent findings suggest that tra i protagonisti al Social Football Summit 2026 di Torino che si è svolgo qualche giorno fa, Piero Ausilio non ha nascosto il desiderio di misurarsi in un altro campionato dopo 28 anni di Inter, quel campionato è la Premier League. "Dopo tanti anni in un'unica squadra, il desiderio che ho è di misurarmi in un campionato diverso e la Premier League rappresenta il progetto più affascinante. Questo non vuol dire che ci sia l'opportunità di andarci dall'oggi al domani, però è sicuramente qualcosa che mi interessa e la prenderei in considerazione", aveva detto l'ex ds nerazzurro. Per Ausilio l'opportunità di lavorare in Premier potrebbe arrivare molto presto e c'è già la squadra pronta ad accoglierlo, il Tottenham.

"I colpi Vicario-Sarr, chiusi con formule più che vantaggiose sul gong del mercato, quando i bianconeri si erano visti sfilare le primissime scelte per centrocampo e porta. Il tutto, grazie all’intermediazione di un agente del calibro di Edoardo Crnjar, che ha contribuito - e non poco - a rinsaldare il legame tra Tottenham e Juve. Ecco, la sensazione è che per l’imminente sessione di mercato invernale, data l’emergenza in due ruoli chiave della rosa, Carnevali possa percorrere il medesimo sentiero. Specie ora che gli Spurs si preparano ad accogliere Piero Ausilio: l’accordo con l’ex ds nerazzurro è a un passo".

BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND - AUGUST 26: Tottenham Hotspur's Destiny Udogie during the Premier League match between AFC Bournemouth and Tottenham Hotspur at Vitality Stadium on August 26, 2023 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Luke Walker/Getty Images).

Il feeling con RDZ non è mia scattato, come dimostrano le 5 presenze raccolte dall’ex Verona in Premier League. Man City MUST stop the rot, old rivals Chelsea and Leeds set for Stamford Bridge blockbuster and Mauricio Pochettino's baptism of fire: SEVEN reasons we're excited for the return of the Premier League

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1437 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • After a thrilling international break that saw England record an historic 3-2 win over Spain our focus returns to the Premier League.
  • It has been revealed that and what a weekend we have coming up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026.

After a thrilling international break that saw England record an historic 3-2 win over Spain our focus returns to the Premier League.

It has been revealed that and what a weekend we have coming up. Old gaffers in new colours, fierce rivalries and some seminal fixtures in the context of the whole season.

With so much to look forward to this weekend, Daily Mail Sport looks over the key reasons to be excited for the return of the world's most electric league.

After a flying start to the campaign Manchester City have begun to run into serious problems under Enzo Maresca and have lost their last three Premier League games on the trot.

And after a particularly humiliating defeat away to Nottingham Forest, who hadn't scored at home before the Cityzens' visit, Maresca and his squad will be desperate for three points especially with champions Arsenal now six points clear.

Sources indicate that city have a good opportunity to turn things around, though, as they host a Fulham side who have endured a terrible run of form against Saturday’s opponents. In fact, the Cottagers have failed to beat City in their last 20 Premier League meetings - a run stretching back 14 years.

But, as ever in the Premier League, nothing is guaranteed and Alvaro Arbeloa’s side are showing promising signs - having enjoyed an unbeaten run in their past four games.

Enzo Maresca's side started in scintillating form but have lost their last three games.

Bonfire night has only just passed but don’t be surprised to see fireworks in west London on Saturday as old rivals Chelsea and Leeds do battle at Stamford Bridge.

After comfortably surviving in their returning year last season, Leeds have kicked on and have quietly emerged as a strong contender for European football. Daniel Farke’s side currently sit ninth, just two points off fifth place Chelsea.

The Blues on the other hand have endured a stuttering, frustrating start to the season. Xabi Alonso’s heralded front three of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro have showcased their terrifying attacking prowess, but the Blues boss’ mystifying tinkering, plus inconsistent performances, has seen his side drop points against Spurs and Sunderland.

However, form will go out of the window as this rivalry - 55 years in the making - is reignited.

Chelsea will be hoping for a repeat of their 6-3 win over Leeds in the league cup this season but Daniel Farke's men will not be as easy to get past in the league.

After Pierre Sage’s dismal start to life in south London, the Crystal Palace board did not hang around and gave the Frenchman the boot after just five months in charge.

And the Eagles have made sure to replace him with someone who has Premier League pedigree, Thomas Frank.

Now while recent memories of the Danish gaffer are almost universally negative it is easy to forget that before his calamitous stint at Tottenham he worked wonders down in west London for Brentford.

And he has every chance of doing the same at Selhurst Park. The job will be far from easy as his new team currently sit rock bottom of the league, but considering Frank’s high pressing and wide set playstyle, Palace’s squad looks a good fit for the Dane.

His first game back will be a tough test, away to Frank Lampard’s resurgent Coventry, but Frank - and the travelling Palace contingent - will be hoping for a newly introduced manager bounce in the east Midlands.

Thomas Frank returns to London to take charge of a struggling Crystal Palace side.

With City faltering and Liverpool and Chelsea failing to hit their stride, the Premier League title race is fast developing into a one-horse competition - and Mikel Arteta will not care one bit.

The Spaniard’s well-oiled machine looks near impossible to stop but as Brighton proved before the last international break, they are not infallible and are set for a tough test returning from the latest break.

The Gunners travel to St James’ Park to take on Newcastle in what promises to be another thriller.

In years past the trip up north has proved to be a banana skin for Arsenal and Arteta, losing four out of their last six games there.

However, Newcastle fans fear their side are fast becoming a fading force and the trip to the North East isn’t perhaps as intimidating as it once was. After all, the Gunners picked up a stoppage time win there last season on their way to the title.

Mikel Arteta's side are hitting their stride but face a tough test at St James' Park.

The surprise package of the season has undoubtedly been Fabian Hurzeler’s high-flying Seagulls who are perched in second place after 10 excellent games.

Recent findings suggest that they remain the only side to have beaten the champions Arsenal and are the league’s top scorers by five goals. They are efficient, fun to watch and have scored a plethora of absolute scorchers this season, but the question on everyone’s lips is: can they keep it up?

History would suggest that overperforming teams tend to settle into the pack after a fast start, and end up battling it out for a coveted spot in a lesser European competition.

But somehow this year it feels different. Brighton appear to have everything they might need to maintain this form and seriously challenge for a Champions League place.

In a recent development, the squad has depth and dynamism with a littany of players boasting youthful exuberance, sprinkled with the experience of the ever-reliable Lewis Dunk and the resurgent Pascal Gross. Crucially, they have a top, motivated manager hellbent on breaking the mould.

Upon return from the break Brighton travel a stubborn Hull side, for their first ever top flight meeting between the two sides.

Brighton have been truly sensational in the opening ten games but can they keep this up going into the notoriously tough winter period.

It seems that after nearly 18 months at Liverpool Florian Wirtz is finally beginning to perform.

After a dismal first year in England in which he only registered nine goals and assists in 33 Premier League games the £116million man is starting to rediscover the form that earned him that valuation.

He enjoyed possibly his best performance in a red shirt just before the break, scoring and assisting in a 3-1 away win against Crystal Palace, and has taken that form into his international performances.

The attacking midfielder got one against Serbia in a routine 3-1 win as well as netting a brace in a 5-0 drubbing of the Netherlands - with one of his strikes an absolute pearler.

The Kop will hope this is the precursor to Wirtz seriously hitting form in the Premier League but the 23-year-old still has a lot to do before he repays the money Liverpool paid for him last year.

Florian Wirtz looks in the mood after a couple of excellent performances for Germany under ex-Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp.

According to recent reports, there is no skirting around the biggest story of the international break - the psychodrama at Manchester United. The two-week break saw the Red Devils wave goodbye to Michael Carrick and say hello to Mauricio Pochettino, hoping the incoming Argentinian will inspire a much-needed turnaround.

After an emotional press conference in which he mentioned goodbye to the US men’s national team, who he has managed for the last two years, the former Spurs and Chelsea boss is tasked with getting his newly introduced club out of the relegation places and finding some much-needed stability.

And it will be a baptism of fire for the 54-year-old, who takes his strugglers to the Anfield cauldron on Sunday, to face a Liverpool side who will have to travel to Anfield, to face a Liverpool side already 10 points ahead.

Factor in the history and rivalry this fixture holds and we are in for a cracker on Merseyside. The smart money would be on Liverpool but as we have seen so many times before a new manager bounce can transform a team in a matter of hours.

And that is all he will have to prepare his charges for their trip to Liverpool - with the new boss landing in Manchester on Wednesday morning to begin work straightaway. Welcome back, Pochettino.

Poch is back and this time in red but he will have his work cut out for him managing a dysfunctional United side at the moment sat in 18th.

Industry observers note that nel corso del consueto appuntamento con il suo editoriale per TMW, Niccolò Ceccarini ha fatto il punto sul calciomercato in entrata del Milan, pronto a prendersi la scena anche a gennaio. Di seguito le sue parole:.

"Il Milan vuole essere protagonista non solo in campionato ma anche sul mercato. Cardinale ha in mente investimenti sia per il presente che per il futuro. L’obiettivo è fare una squadra sempre più forte che possa lottare il prima possibile per lo scudetto. Il difensore centrale resta la priorità. Gonçalo Inacio dello Sporting Lisbona è il preferito. Il Milan è consapevole che serviranno 40 milioni di euro ma è pronto a fare un maxi investimento. Molto dipenderà dalla volontà del club portoghese. Tra le alternative da non trascurare anche Sylla dell’Union Saint-Gilloise, Ganiou del Lens e Reggiani del Borussia Dortmund. L’idea del Milan è quella di incrementare sempre di più il livello tecnico, soprattutto la prossima estate. Qui i progetti non mancano: ci sono due obiettivi e un sogno. Per l’attacco, ormai non è più un segreto, i riflettori si sono accesi da tempo su Tresoldi. Quasi impossibile che a gennaio il Brugge possa aprire una trattativa. I rossoneri stanno gettando le basi per arrivare a giugno davanti a tutti anche se la concorrenza è tanta. Al Milan servirà anche un grande centrocampista che possa in parte compensare il probabile addio di Luka Modric. Il nome giusto è quello di Angelo Stiller, classe 2001 dello Stoccarda e nazionale tedesco. Ha caratteristiche simili al campione croato, molti estimatori sul mercato ed una clausola rescissoria da 40 milioni di euro. Il sogno invece si chiama Bruno Fernandes. Il capitano del Manchester United è in scadenza di contratto e deve ancora decidere il suo futuro. Tra lui e Amorim c’è un ottimo rapporto e in più l’operazione potrebbe essere resa possibile anche dalla voglia di tornare a giocare in Italia. Ed è qui che il Milan si è subito messo alla finestra, pronto a cogliere l’occasione [...]".

L’ex giocatore ricorda i rimproveri nello spogliatoio del Milan e gli scherzi organizzati con Pirlo.

Massimo Oddo indica in Gennaro Gattuso il principale artefice del primato della Lazio in Serie A. L’ex giocatore biancoceleste e del Milan ha parlato del rapporto con l’amico ed ex compagno di squadra in un’intervista a Repubblica. Oltre al giudizio sull’attuale allenatore della Lazio, ha ricordato il ruolo che aveva nello spogliatoio rossonero e alcuni episodi vissuti insieme.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Secondo Oddo, l’esperienza da commissario tecnico della Nazionale, conclusa senza la qualificazione ai Mondiali, ha inciso sulla consapevolezza di Gattuso. Non ne avrebbe però cambiato il modo di essere: «Gattuso non cambia, migliora. Da ct, mancando la qualificazione ai Mondiali, ha subito una delle lezioni sportive più grandi della sua carriera, non solo per il risultato. Adesso ha preso ancora più consapevolezza di prima».

Sources indicate that oddo riconosce nell’allenatore della Lazio un ruolo che aveva già ai tempi del Milan: «ma è sempre stato un “braccio armato” pronto a intervenire e risolvere i momenti di crisi. Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4619 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.
  • Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

According to recent reports, palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”.

Sources indicate that "Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

It has been revealed that chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

In a recent development, palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

In a recent development, it looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as major of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

Sources indicate that cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ.

According to recent reports, “Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, mentioned. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”.

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

Reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

Recent findings suggest that "This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX.

As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz.

That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

Recent findings suggest that reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who noted: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

Sources indicate that “I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”.

Industry observers note that goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

Conor Coady was impressed with that Mike Penders double save in the first half 👏 pic.twitter.com/6NJqFDvnzk.

But the Belgian flapped at the corner, which gave Harry Wilson a second chance to get his delivery right. And he did just that by finding Muharemovic at the back post to head the ball into the net.

Sources indicate that valentín Barco survived Alonso’s changes, but was partly at fault for Leeds’s second goal just after the break. He lost the ball and Ethan Ampadu galloped away from Rogers before crossing. Lukas Nmecha got the slightest of touches and Aaronsen smashed the ball into the net.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav.

The substitutes then took over, as Chelsea shocked the visitors before Leeds substitute Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave his team hope by reducing the deficit with 15 minutes remaining.

Any thoughts of a Leeds comeback were promptly erased, however, as Barco netted his first Chelsea goal from a Rogers pass, which may have taken a slight touch to deny him a fourth assist in the record books. Welbeck added a sixth in time added on.

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9.

Recent findings suggest that on the defeat by Chelsea, Farke mentioned: “The referee had the idea to give a penalty. No one in the stadium was asking for it, no one of their players was asking for it, but he spotted a situation where he thought he would give a penalty.

“All of a sudden they scored the goal, then their players came into the game at half-time, the whole stadium after being relatively quiet for 60 minutes they of course were there then. The momentum was all of a sudden on their side. In football small situations can change the whole momentum of a game and this happened.”.

"100% I meant it!" 😅Morgan Rogers claims he is really enjoying his football after he helped Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/7uUQb6eIla.

Here’s a reminder of the assist in question. Did Rogers mean it? Let us know in the comments beneath this live blog...

It has been revealed that TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

On the message from the manager at half-time, Palmer told Sky Sports: “Just up the intensity, play a bit more, become more alive because I think the first half was flat, everyone agreed in the changing room, so we stepped up.

It has been revealed that asked whether Alonso’s message was delivered calmly, he remarked: “At the start, but then he got a bit angry. But it was alright.”.

On Chelsea’s half-time changes, Conor Coady remarked on Sky Sports: “I think the credit goes down to [Alonso]. He made a bit of a statement by doing that at half-time. Four subs is a lot to do at half-time but it was needed. Listen, we said about the first half that it was kind of like the players hadn’t played with each other, and then the significant guns came on... They were electric at times.”.

Sources indicate that A crazy match which was decided by Chelsea’s superb substitutes. Alonso took action at half-time and was rewarded with six goals in a madcap second half. Palmer hauled Chelsea back into the game, Rogers collected a handful of assists and Neto scored the go-ahead goal. You wonder what this match will do for the likes of Estevao and Gittens, though.

Chelsea 6 Leeds United 3 (Welbeck) Pure reflexes from Welbeck, who diverts Barco’s wild effort beyond Zetterer.

Palmer has the hat-trick ball on his mind and attempts an audacious chip but just gets his angles wrong. Any guesses who laid on the chance? Rogers. Of course.

Leeds look to break but Wilson mistimes his run and is caught offside.

There will be six minutes of time added on.

A tap on Barco’s head from Wilson provokes some histrionics from the Argentine but Jarred Gillett calms all parties down.

Industry observers note that leeds are still pushing. Stach’s effort from eight yards out is closed down before Tanaka’s strike from the edge of the box is smothered by James.

Alonso goes into the book, apparently for straying too far outside of his technical area.

Chelsea 5 Leeds United 3 (Barco) Rogers lays on his fourth assist of the match, driving towards the byline before flashing a searching ball across the face of goal which Barco spears past Zetterer at the far post. That should be that, right?

According to recent reports, valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9.

We could be in for a blockbuster finish.

What a tie this has turned into!

Leeds win a corner, which falls to Stach on the edge of the box but his effort is charged down.

Industry observers note that it will be a source of acute anguish for Farke that Chelsea’s fourth goal came before he could make his four changes: Stach, Calvert-Lewin, Tanaka and Okafor eventually replace James, Nmecha, Longstaff and Aaronson. Conversely, it should be to Alonso’s credit that he took action early - his substitutes have decided this tie.

According to recent reports, chelsea 4 Leeds United 2 (Welbeck) Rogers gallops on to a simple ball down the right channel and his cutback (towards Palmer) is picked up by Welbeck who spins before firing beyond Zetterer, leaving three Leeds defenders sprawled in front of him. He cares not, and absorbs the love of the crowd in the near corner.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz.

It has been revealed that palmer goes close after having found a yard of space on the edge of the box. His strike spears through a thicket of limbs in Leeds’ box but Zetterer pulls off a strong save to deny the Englishman a quickfire hat-trick.

According to recent reports, chelsea 3 Leeds United 2 (Neto) Just 11 minutes after going 2-0 down, Chelsea find themselves ahead. Palmer threads a through-ball through the middle for Rogers, who slides in front of his marker to an open Neto who sweeps the ball beyond Zetterer. Leeds punished for leaving themselves two vs two at the back there.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX.

Chelsea have got their tails up and Palmer almost lays on a go-ahead goal but James cannot turn in his cross from the left.

Acheampong’s throw-in is knocked down by Rogers into the path of Palmer who works in from the right, passing the ball around a Leeds defender and past a rooted Zetterer.

Industry observers note that TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

Chavarria is caught by James in the box and the referee points to the spot. That came from nowhere.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea 0 Leeds United 2 (Aaronson) Amapadu deserves so much credit here. He steals the ball from Barco high, bursts beyond Rogers on the right and while Nmecha cannot turn in his cutback, Aaronson arrives late to stroke the ball past Penders and double Leeds’ lead.

Justin, James and Wilson have got a lot of joy down Leeds’ right, rotating in Chavarria’s orbit. It has been difficult for Chelsea to pin them down and Gittens’ attacking threat has been blunted as he attempts to track their movements.

Leeds supporters boo Argentina World Cup squad member Barco’s every touch, and another Leeds foul, this time Justin on Gittens, prompts a second Chelsea free-kick.

As recently as March, a giant mural of Estêvão Willian appeared on the side of a building outside Stamford Bridge as the teenager threatened to become Chelsea’s number one poster boy.

He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

But inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

Industry observers note that estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha.

Much has been made of Chelsea’s willingness to let the opposition have the ball under Xabi Alonso, but tonight they will likely be forced to dictate proceedings. In Leeds, they face one of only two sides who have completed fewer passes than them in the Premier League.

Industry observers note that asked how he will approach the Carabao Cup this season, Daniel Farke noted: “We’ll try to win it. That’s the quickest way to Europe and to some glory. Of course knowing that the Premier League will always have the priority and knowing that we are as successful as possible there, especially to reach our first goal to establish ourselves [at] this level.

It has been revealed that “We are not the favourites to win the Carabao Cup, we know this. Challenging, difficult games, but of course we travel to London in order to go through in the next round without doing anything stupid at this stage of the campaign because you also have to rotate a bit more and integrate a few new players. Nevertheless, we want to be at our best and anyhow possible we also want to go through to the next round.”.

Tonight represents an opportunity for 16-year-old Reggie Watson to announce himself at senior level. The central-midfielder caught Alonso’s eye during pre-season when the Spaniard mentioned of him: “Reggie Watson, a great midfielder. He thinks, he’s very collective, he’s very generous on the effort, intelligent with the ball”.

“For his age, I’m really impressed with him.”.

Sources indicate that good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

In Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate new players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

Alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:38 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Andy Robertson notes he fully understands why the Tartan Army are increasingly concerned about where the team are going under Sebastien Pocognoli.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:38 EST, 17 November 2026.

Andy Robertson notes he fully understands why the Tartan Army are increasingly concerned about where the team are going under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Monday’s heavy defeat to Switzerland marked the conclusion of a dismal Nations League campaign which saw the Belgian’s men beat only North Macedonia across six matches to finish a distant third.

After the high of qualifying for the World Cup a year ago, supporters have been brought crashing back to earth since the summer with signs of progress proving hard to come by under the new manager.

When the full-time whistle blew in St Gallen to confirm a 4-0 loss, there were audible jeers from the travelling fans.

Skipper Robertson has no concern with what he heard and knows the players have a job on their hands to turn the situation round.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I can understand why they’re concerned. I can understand why they’re frustrated,’ he said. ‘I can understand why the away fans didn’t really want us to go over and applaud them.

Robertson can't hide anguish after 4-0 loss on what was his record breaking 103rd cap.

According to recent reports, ‘I can completely understand that. I’ve been around a long time now and unfortunately I’ve had these nights a couple of times where the fans do react like that.

‘You have to let them do that and you also understand why they’re doing it. But I suppose if we’re trying to flip a positive on it, I think maybe the first five or six games under Steve Clarke were maybe similar where we had a lot of change in the squad, we were trying to build something, we were trying to integrate new people into a new squad and things like that.

‘We’re trying to do that and we have to be positive about that. We need the young lads to feel comfortable around us. We need them to step up.

Industry observers note that ‘We need the older players to really help them in that and really, really step up. And that’s the only way we’re going to be successful.

Sources indicate that ‘We’ll still be positive because that’s the only way we know, and we know we can build something special. We’ve done it. We’ve been questioned a few times and bounced back and now we’re going to need to do it again with a newer squad.’.

Robertson admits that the adverse results have fed into a lack of harmony behind the scenes — a sharp contrast to the positivity which was palpable as the side qualified for the World Cup a year ago today.

Robertson understands why fans booed another dismal performance by Pocognoli's team.

‘I still think we need to work on it,’ he noted. ‘We still need to get closer as a group again because — I don’t like looking at the past any more — but under Steve we had a really close-knit group where what we created was pretty special.

In a recent development, ‘And that’s rare but we also have to try and do that again and we’re trying to make the new players and the young lads feel as comfortable as possible. That’s the role of the older players and we have to keep doing that.

‘We have to keep encouraging them because they’re the ones that want to take us forward in years to come and they’re also the ones that are going to help us now.

‘Us older lads, we need to put a lot of responsibility on (ourselves) to try and help them do that, to try and keep pushing them, and we have to keep stepping up as well.

‘As a collective, we all need to step up more and if we do that then hopefully we can be successful again.’.

While the spotlight has largely fallen on the manager for persisting with a 3-4-2-1 formation, Robertson is adamant that it’s only fair the blame is shared around.

Sources indicate that ‘We all have to take responsibility,’ he said. ‘Tactics and the way the manager sets us up and everything like that is one thing but then you’ve got 11  players, and we had 16 players, who have to go out and perform.

Skipper Robertson roars with anger and disbelief as Scotland team crumbles in Switzerland.

‘I don’t think we performed as a collective good enough. When you get beat 4-0, there’s not going to be any positives. There’s no fan in this stadium that’s going to go home and go: “We played well in the first half”.

Industry observers note that ‘That’s not how football works and we’re very aware of that. I’m very aware of that in terms of I don’t take any positives from a 4-0 defeat. I’m sorry but that’s the way I am and unfortunately that’s the way it is.’.

The Tottenham man became Scotland’s most capped player on Monday when he pulled on the jersey for the 103rd time, but that achievement was scant consolation at the time.

‘I’ve not given myself the chance to reflect,’ insisted Robertson. ‘In a couple of days’ time, probably when I unlock my phone and I get a couple of messages, I’ll realise what I’ve achieved and I don’t take it for granted.

Sources indicate that ‘I don’t take the magnitude of it for granted either, being able to overtake the legend of Kenny Dalglish. But it’s very hard to focus on myself after a result like that. I always focus on the team first and that’s always been my way.’.

Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s newly introduced-look midfield

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Industry observers note that little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

Sources indicate that united’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq.

“It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick said. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

In a recent development, united probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game initiative.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

It has been revealed that mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick said. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”.

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m.

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”.

Sources indicate that carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick mentioned. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”.

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00.

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q.

Fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

Job done. Now a much bigger test awaits.

“Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another big one on Sunday.”.

It has been revealed that 81 - Kobbie Mainoo completed the most passes in Manchester United's 4-0 win over Sabah (81).It was the most by an Englishman for the Red Devils in a UEFA Champions League match since Michael Carrick in February 2014 vs Olympiakos (89).Mentor. pic.twitter.com/59wSvQydOG.

Benjamin Šeško and Patrick Dorgu share their thoughts after Manchester United's successful return to Champions League football ✅🎙️ @OliviaBuzaglo | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/iKC58Po2Vx.

Michael Carrick is going to make his final two changes of the night as youngsters Lacey and Amass come on.

Industry observers note that michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

Sources indicate that it must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

As we speak, there have just been two goals scored in the last few moments in the two early kick-offs. Both home sides, Fenerbahce and PSV, have just equalised in their respective games.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥.

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Industry observers note that manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick stated. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

According to recent reports, “I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the new challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”.

According to recent reports, sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.
